title: Mood differential and longitudinal course mastery check

items.prompt: An invented file. K. is 41, a delivery driver, and describes seven months of low mood, loss of interest, waking two hours early, and eating less. K. takes a beta blocker started three years ago for migraine and prednisolone started five weeks ago for a chest problem. K. drinks at weekends only, unchanged for years. K. attends alone. Asked about earlier periods, K. says there was a spell in the twenties when everything was easy and money went quickly, but K. cannot date it and is not sure it lasted more than a couple of days. K.'s brother is described as 'up and down' with no further detail. No physical symptoms are recorded and no examination or blood test has been done. Rank the unipolar, bipolar-spectrum, medical, neurologic, medication, substance, grief, trauma, and contextual alternatives for K. For every one, give its state as supported, countered, unassessed, or not answerable from history, and give the evidence or the absence that puts it there.

answer.correct: Unipolar depressive course: supported, on the seven-month picture. Bipolar-spectrum: live on two weak items, an undated and possibly very brief period of ease and free spending reported by K. alone, and a brother described as up and down with no detail; both are single-channel and both are confirmable, so the state is supported but not established, and the undated brevity means no duration convention can be applied to it at all. Medication: supported and the strongest medical-side item, because prednisolone was started five weeks ago and the mood picture is seven months old, so the steroid cannot have started it but the timing of any change five weeks ago should be asked about; the beta blocker at three years is temporally uninformative for a seven-month change. Medical: not answerable from history, since no examination and no blood test have been done; the file records no physical symptoms, which is weaker than a normal result. Substance: countered as an initiator, because weekend-only drinking is unchanged for years, and it remains worth dating. Contextual: unassessed, since nothing about K.'s work pattern, sleep opportunity, or circumstances is recorded. Neurologic: unassessed rather than countered, because no neurological history, examination or cognitive enquiry appears. Grief: unassessed. Trauma: unassessed.
answer.summary: One supported alternative, one live but unestablished, one supported medication item whose chronology is partly against it, one substance item countered as an initiator, one not answerable from history, and four unassessed.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for placing unipolar and bipolar-spectrum with their evidence, including the observation that K.'s remembered spell is undated and possibly brief so no duration convention can be applied to it. Award one point for the medication reasoning: prednisolone is recent and cannot have started a seven-month picture while remaining worth asking about, and a drug started three years ago carries no temporal argument for a seven-month change. Award one point for correctly separating countered from unassessed, which requires substance to be countered as an initiator on the unchanged pattern, and neurologic, grief, trauma and contextual to be unassessed rather than low. Award one point for recording the medical alternative as not answerable from history and for stating that an absence of recorded physical symptoms is not a negative examination. A response that writes 'no history of trauma' or 'no medical cause' as findings loses the third and fourth points, because that is the specific error the lesson repairs. On a retry, rank a different invented file: a 27-year-old with five months of low mood, an aunt with a mood disorder of unspecified type, isotretinoin started six months ago, a partner attending who describes a fortnight last year of very little sleep and constant plans, and no bloods taken.
acceptableResponses: Any response that assigns all nine alternatives a state from the four, attaches the evidence or the absence that justifies each, distinguishes countered from unassessed, and treats the undated brief spell as evidence too weak to carry a duration argument.
commonErrors: Recording unassessed alternatives as negative findings
Treating prednisolone as the explanation because steroids are associated with mood change, without checking that the mood picture predates it by months
Applying a duration threshold to an episode K. cannot date
Calling the medical alternative countered because no physical symptoms are recorded
Ranking by how common each condition is rather than by the evidence in the file

items.prompt: Take one line from K.'s file: 'a spell in the twenties when everything was easy and money went quickly; K. cannot date it and is not sure it lasted more than a couple of days.' Write three short paragraphs. First, its weight if it happened as described. Second, its channel, naming the specific bias that applies to this kind of content and what is known about how strong that bias is. Third, the second channel you would seek and what it would and would not settle. Then answer in one sentence: does the reported brevity of the spell make it less informative, and why?

answer.correct: Weight: high if true, because a period of elevated or activated mood that was a change from K.'s usual state would move the presentation from a depressive episode to a depressive episode in a bipolar-spectrum course, which changes the expected course and the questions asked at every later contact. Channel: weak. A single undated retrospective self-report, given while depressed, about a kind of state that people under-recognise; in one general-population reappraisal only about a fifth of people with a research diagnosis of bipolar disorder recognised having had hypomanic or manic episodes, and the commonest explanations offered were that the periods had been pleasant and productive or felt like part of the person's personality. Milder and briefer episodes are the hardest to recall, and this one is reported as both. Second channel: an informant who knew K. in that period, with K.'s consent, asked whether the state was a visible change from K.'s usual self and how long it ran. That would improve the reliability of the report and would still not establish a diagnosis. Brevity: reported brevity lowers what the item can support under the duration convention in widest use, and it is a weaker argument than it looks, because that four-day minimum entered practice with DSM-IV in 1994, a research-criteria group states no empirical evidence supports the particular cut-off and proposes two days, and others hold that lowering it would widen bipolar diagnosis; here the deeper problem is that K. cannot date the spell at all, so no threshold can be applied to it either way.
answer.summary: High weight, weak channel with a named and quantified under-recognition bias, an informant as the second channel, and a brevity argument that turns out to be blocked by the absence of a date.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for a weight statement that says what the item would reclassify rather than merely calling it important. Award one point for a channel statement that names retrospective under-recognition of elevated states and gives the study's scale and limits, including that the finding describes people who have the condition and cannot be read backwards as a diagnostic sign. Award one point for a second channel that is a person and a specific question, together with an honest statement that it improves reliability without establishing a diagnosis. Award one point for the last sentence only if it both reports that the duration convention is contested and notices that an undated spell cannot be tested against any threshold. A response that treats the four-day convention as settled, in either direction, does not earn the fourth point. On a retry, do the same for a line reading: 'partner reports a fortnight last year of very little sleep and constant plans, which the partner found alarming.' Notice that the channel is now the strong one and the weight statement barely changes.
acceptableResponses: Any response that separates weight from channel, quantifies or bounds the under-recognition bias from the lesson's evidence, proposes a specific informant question as the second channel, and identifies the missing date as the reason no duration argument can run.
commonErrors: Collapsing weight and channel into a single verdict on the item
Reading low self-recognition backwards, so that a warmly described past week becomes evidence of hypomania
Applying the four-day convention as though it were settled
Proposing 'further history from the patient' as the second channel, which is the same channel again
Claiming an informant account would confirm the diagnosis

items.prompt: Still on K.'s file. Write the four requests you would make before the next contact. For each, state which two alternatives it separates, what each possible result would mean, and one thing it would not settle. Then write the two-sentence entry you would leave in the record about what is missing, in a form that tells the next reader which questions were asked and which were not.

answer.correct: A defensible set: an informant account of the spell in K.'s twenties and of any similar period, which separates unipolar from bipolar-spectrum, where a description of a visible change from usual self raises the second and no recollection leaves the first where it is; it would not date the spell reliably. Detail of the brother's 'up and down', which separates the same two, where a confirmed bipolar diagnosis in a first-degree relative raises the bipolar-spectrum alternative and a different or absent diagnosis removes a weak pointer; it says nothing about K.'s own course. Physical examination and basic bloods including thyroid function, which separates medical from psychiatric alternatives, where a normal result removes an alternative and a raised thyroid-stimulating hormone with normal free thyroxine starts an argument instead of ending one, because that pattern is common in tested depressed people and has not been shown to cause or worsen depression; it would not explain the seven months. A dated medication history covering the prednisolone start and any dose changes, which separates a medication-related from an independent picture, where a step change in mood at the start or at a dose change supports the drug and a mood picture unchanged across both leaves it aside; association alone would still not establish cause. Asking about losses, trauma, work pattern and sleep opportunity is a fifth legitimate answer and may replace any of the above if it is argued. The record entry must say which questions were put and which were not, for example: 'Loss, trauma, neurological history and work pattern were not covered at this contact and are not recorded either way. No examination or blood test has been done; the absence of recorded physical symptoms is an absence of enquiry, not a negative finding.'
answer.summary: Four requests, each tied to the pair of alternatives it separates, with the meaning of each possible result and an explicit limit, plus a record entry that distinguishes questions not asked from findings that were negative.
answer.reasoning: Award one point for requests that are each attached to a named pair of alternatives rather than listed as general workup. Award one point for stating what each possible result would mean in both directions, including the thyroid result whose mildly abnormal form does not supply an explanation. Award one point for a stated limit on each request, since a request presented as decisive is the error this item tests. Award one point for a record entry that a later reader could use to tell an unasked question from a negative finding. Any response whose record entry could be read as 'no history of trauma' does not earn the fourth point. On a retry, write the requests for the invented 27-year-old described in the first item's retry, where the partner is present and the drug is recent.
acceptableResponses: Any four defensible requests, each naming the pair of alternatives it separates, the meaning of each possible result, and a stated limit, with a record entry that separates unasked questions from negative findings.
commonErrors: Listing investigations as a routine panel with no alternative attached
Treating a mildly raised thyroid-stimulating hormone as an explanation for the depressive picture
Writing a record entry that reads as a negative finding for a question nobody asked
Naming only what would confirm an alternative and not what would lower it
Recommending a treatment change as the discriminating step

items.prompt: In an invented file, M. has had low mood and early waking for six months and has drunk heavily every evening for the last six weeks, saying it is to get to sleep. After four weeks of observed abstinence during an unrelated hospital admission, M.'s mood has clearly improved and the early waking is unchanged. Which reading does the evidence best support?

options.text: The unchanged early waking shows the depressive picture is independent of the drinking, because a symptom that survives abstinence cannot be alcohol-related.

The mood response is informative and the unchanged sleep is much less so, because sleep disturbance commonly persists for months into abstinence, so the two symptoms answer to abstinence on different timescales and give two results rather than one.
The improvement over four weeks shows the whole presentation was alcohol-related, since most symptoms resolve within the first four weeks of abstinence.
Nothing can be concluded, because six weeks of heavy drinking is too short a period for any chronology argument to apply.

answer.summary: Abstinence produces two results on two timescales; the mood response carries information and the unchanged sleep carries much less.
answer.reasoning: Abstinence is one intervention and the two symptoms respond to it differently. Most symptoms resolve within the first four weeks of abstinence, which is why the two-to-four-week observation period is advised, so a clear mood improvement across four weeks is a real result. Sleep is the documented exception: for close to half of people with alcohol dependence it stays disturbed for months after the last drink, so unchanged early waking is weak evidence in either direction. The first option treats an exception as a rule. The third overreads the mood improvement and ignores the six-month lead of the mood picture over the six-week escalation, which argues against the drinking having started it. The fourth abandons a chronology argument that has usable dates on both sides. If you chose the first or third, write both symptom timelines out separately against the abstinence date before answering. On a retry, decide the same question for a file where the mood is unchanged after four weeks and the early waking has settled.
commonErrors: Treating any symptom that survives abstinence as proof of an independent disorder
Reading improvement across an abstinence period as proof that alcohol caused everything
Merging the mood result and the sleep result into a single verdict
Discarding a chronology argument that has dates available on both sides

rubrics.title: Ranking a differential by the evidence in the file

criteria.description: Places the unipolar and bipolar-spectrum alternatives with the evidence that puts them there, and notes that an undated, possibly very brief remembered spell cannot carry a duration argument.
Reasons about the two drugs by chronology: a five-week-old steroid cannot have started a seven-month picture yet is worth asking about, and a three-year-old drug carries no temporal argument for it.
Separates countered from unassessed correctly across substance, neurologic, grief, trauma, and contextual alternatives.
Records the medical alternative as not answerable from history and states that no recorded physical symptoms is an absence of enquiry rather than a negative examination.

rubrics.title: Judging one item of longitudinal history

criteria.description: States what the item would reclassify if true, rather than asserting that it is important.
Names the under-recognition of past elevated states as the channel bias, bounds it with the lesson's evidence, and does not read that evidence backwards as a diagnostic sign.
Proposes a specific person and a specific question as the second channel, and states that it improves reliability without establishing a diagnosis.
Reports the duration convention as contested and identifies the missing date as the reason no threshold argument can run on this item at all.

rubrics.title: Naming what would separate two alternatives

criteria.description: Each request names the pair of alternatives it separates instead of being listed as general workup.
States what each possible result would mean in both directions, including a mildly abnormal thyroid result that does not supply an explanation.
Gives each request an explicit limit, so that none is presented as decisive.
Writes a record entry from which a later reader can tell an unasked question from a negative finding.

rubrics.title: Reading an abstinence period as two results

criteria.description: Selects the reading in which the mood response and the sleep response are two results on different timescales.
Rejects both the reading that a surviving symptom proves independence and the reading that improvement proves the drinking caused everything.
